title: Entropy mismatch in routing policy caused incorrect variant handoff — action items
creator: Maya Chen
description: Post-incident work to remediate an event where routing policy entropy calculations went out of sync with runtime metadata, producing an invalid variant selection path for a subset of requests. This ticket collects root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and medium-term platform fixes to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-08 02:13 UTC a subset of inference requests were routed to an incompatible model variant due to a divergence between policy entropy seeds and runtime tag assignments after a config reload. The mismatch caused spiky error rates and elevated latency for affected shards until traffic was manually shifted to a fallback pool at 02:41 UTC. Impact: ~3% of requests to the EU region over a 28-minute window experienced degraded responses or retries.
timeline: 2026-03-08 02:12 UTC: Rolling config update for policy weights began (canary batch 1)
2026-03-08 02:13 UTC: First error spike observed on EU routing service (elevated 5xx and validation errors)
2026-03-08 02:15 UTC: Auto-retries amplified errors for some clients, telemetry showed inconsistent variant_tag values between planner and router
2026-03-08 02:22 UTC: On-call invoked manual routing policy rollback for canary group
2026-03-08 02:28 UTC: Fallback rules triggered for some tenants to legacy-compat variants; latency improved but error rate remained elevated
2026-03-08 02:41 UTC: Traffic fully shifted to fallback pool and incident declared mitigated
2026-03-08 03:05 UTC: Post-incident logging reveals a race in policy seed recomputation and a missing defensive assert when variant indexes differ
root_cause: A race condition during policy weight recomputation caused the planner to compute entropy-based variant weights using stale seed metadata while the router had already re-tagged some hosts with new variant assignments. The planner and router used different namespaces for the seed derivation after a config reload, producing deterministic-but-incompatible variant picks. There was no end-to-end telemetry assertion to detect seed/variant divergence before routing decisions were executed.
action_items: (P0 Short-term) Add a runtime guard that rejects routing decisions if the planner seed hash != router seed hash; implement immediate fail-open to stable default variant — owner: Diego Alvarez — due: 2026-03-15
(P1 Short-term) Patch the config reload path to double-buffer seed updates and apply atomically across planner/router processes — owner: Priya Patel — due: 2026-03-18

(P1) Add a lightweight invariant check emitted to observability when variant_tag distributions diverge by >1% between planner and router; create Grafana alert — owner: SRE Team (lead: Ahmed Khatri) — due: 2026-03-20

(P2) Create an e2e test in the routing integration harness that simulates concurrent config reloads and verifies variant determinism across a multi-region setup — owner: Katerina Ivanov — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-04-03

(P2 Medium-term) Rework entropy seed derivation to use a single canonical namespace stored in consistent config store (with versioned writes) — owner: Runtime Infra (lead: Lucas Romero) — estimate: 8 — release: runtime-1.22
(P3) Documentation: add operator runbook steps for detecting seed divergence and safe remediation (rollback vs fallback) — owner: Maya Chen — due: 2026-03-25
comments: 2026-03-09 Maya Chen: Initial analysis completed — confirmed planner/router seed mismatch and lack of defensive check in routing agent.
2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez: Spike completed for atomic seed guard; working on integration tests. Found that some older router builds ignore new seed header; adding compatibility shim.
2026-03-11 Priya Patel: Config reload double-buffer design reviewed with infra; suggested adding a short TTL on seed versions to prevent long-lived drift.
2026-03-12 Ahmed Khatri (SRE): Drafted Grafana alert and an accompanying playbook entry; will iterate after PR lands.
2026-03-13 Diego Alvarez: Opened PR for atomic-seed-guard (see links). Next steps: run integration harness and schedule canary rollout during low-traffic window.
